chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

By Allah! Allah did not leave the earth since He took the soul of Adam (peace be upon him), except that in it there was an Imam through whom one is guided to Allah, and he is His proof upon His servants; and the earth cannot remain without an Imam who is a divine authority of Allah upon His servants.

key_terms.حُجَّة: Hujjah — the divine proof or authority; the Imam as God's representative and evidence upon humanity
key_terms.قَبَضَ آدَمَ: He took Adam (his soul) — the starting point marking the beginning of the era of Imamate succession
key_terms.يُهْتَدَى بِهِ: Through whom one is guided — the passive form emphasizes that guidance flows through the Imam

ai.seo_question: Did Imam al-Baqir say the earth is never without an Imam as divine proof?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) affirms the core Shia doctrine of continuous Imamate with a solemn oath: since the death of Adam (AS), Allah has never left the earth without an Imam who serves as the divine guide and proof (hujjah) upon humanity. This teaching — addressed to early Shia Muslims in 2nd century Hijri Medina — established that the Imam's presence is not merely a political matter but a cosmic necessity: the earth requires a divinely appointed representative as the interface between God and creation. The use of the oath 'By Allah!' underscores the absolute doctrinal certainty of this claim.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl, from Abu Hamza, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Allah<sup>azwj</sup> did not Leave the earth since He<sup>azwj</sup> Captured (the soul of) Adam<sup>as</sup>, except therein was an Imam He<sup>azwj</sup> Guided with to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and he was His<sup>azwj</sup> Divine Authority upon His<sup>azwj</sup> servants; and the earth cannot remain without an Imam<sup>asws</sup>, a Divine Authority of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> upon His<sup>azwj</sup> creatures’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from abu Hamza from abu Ja‘far (a.s.) who has said the following.

“I swear to Allah that He has not, from the day Adam died, left the earth without an Imam who would guide people to the Lord as with divine authority over the servants of the Lord. The earth will never remain without an Imam with Divine authority over His servants.”
